public_rationale: Under the stated reading, the categorical claim is too broad. Before the post, researchers had implemented erase-and-check and provided a conditional guarantee against specified adversarial modifications. Its assumptions matter: an independent critique demonstrates a bypass outside the restricted setting. This contradicts the absence of any engineered safety guarantee, but does not establish comprehensive safety. The outcome depends on counting explicit, bounded guarantees.
limitations: The decisive source was a preprint at the time of the post.
The guarantee depends on correct detection of the original harmful prompt and a bounded attack model.
A reading restricted to comprehensive safety would not be contradicted by this evidence.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: No one has ever been able to engineer safety guarantees for generative AI systems.

statement.excerpt: Nobody has ever been able to engineer safety guarantees around then.

our_interpretation: Around then is read as a typographical error for around them, referring to generative AI systems.
A safety guarantee means an engineered assurance that a specified harmful behavior is prevented under stated conditions. Merely lowering observed failure rates does not qualify.
A guarantee may have explicit assumptions and a bounded scope. The words do not require protection against every possible harm, or deployment in a commercial service.
Ever covers work completed through February 21, 2024; the claim supplies no historical starting date.
criteria.support_condition: A sufficiently comprehensive technical record establishes that no implemented, demonstrable safety guarantee for a generative AI system existed by publication.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one pre-publication implemented method provides a valid guarantee of a specified safety property around a generative AI system, with its assumptions and scope made explicit.

evidence.publisher: Aounon Kumar and colleagues via arXiv
evidence.explanation: The paper implements a filter around LLM inputs and establishes protection against bounded token additions when the underlying filter detects the original harmful prompt. That is an engineered, conditional safety guarantee, although it does not certify all prompts or all generated content.

evidence.publisher: Leo Schwinn and colleagues via arXiv
evidence.explanation: The authors demonstrate a bypass using an input outside the defense's restrictive harmful-instruction assumption. This is material evidence against calling the method generally safe; it does not establish failure of the bounded guarantee when its stated assumptions hold.
